The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Sri. Naresh. V S/o Krishna Reddy V. V in the road traffic accident that took place on 19.04.2023.
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the petition are as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that, on 19.04.2023 at about 08.15 a.m., the deceased was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-67-H-5038 on IOC Road, Near Cheemandahalli Gate, Jadigenahalli Hobli, Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District,
slowly, carefully and observing the movement of traffic, at that time a Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-3518 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle. Due to forced impact, deceased fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately after the accident deceased was shifted to Ashwini Hospital for first aid, thereafter shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein injured was admitted as inpatient but inspite of better treatment he died in the Hospital.
Thereafter

body was shifted to Hoskote Government Hospital for postmortem and then the petitioners shifted the dead body to their native place and performed the last rites and obsequies ceremony and they have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and funeral expenses.
On account of the sudden and sad demise of the deceased in the said accident, the petitioners have undergoing deep mental shock and mental agony and hardship.

sentences.text: Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 26 years and working as Safety Officer at Maptec Consultancy and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
The petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased, so the petitioners have lost their family member.
The petitioners were solely depending upon the income of the deceased.
The respondents are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay Rs.75,00,000/- with cost and interest to the petitioners.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
3. After the service of notice, respondent No.2 has not appeared before this.
Hence, placed Exparte.

The respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed his written statement and denied the case of the petitioners as false and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
This respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further this respondent seeks protection u/s 158(6) and 134(C) of M. V. Act.
It is further submitted that, alleged offending vehicle Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-3518 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
Further, the deceased was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.

Further, the driver of offending Eicher Tanker was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident and after investigation police have filed charge-sheet u/s 279 and 304(A) of M. V. Act against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 19.04.2023 at about 08.15 a.m., accident took place on IOC Road, near Cheemandahalli Gate, Jadigenahalli Hobli, Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-3518 as a result deceased has succumbed to the accidental injuries?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In order order to prove the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 got examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 24 and Supervisor at M/s.

Maptec Consultancy Services Pvt.
Ltd., is examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.25 to Ex.P.28.

On the other hand,
Legal Executive of respondent No.1 Insurance Company is examined as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
6.
Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the material placed on record.

7. My findings on the above issues as under:-

V S/o Krishna Reddy V. V met with road traffic accident and died due to rash and negligent driving for driver of Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA- 53-D-3518.

The burden is upon the petitioners to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-3518 .
9.
The petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased Naresh.

V. The claimants/petitioners, in order to prove that, the occurrence of road traffic accident as contended by them in their claim petition has occurred on the date, time and place and in the manner as contended by them in their claim petition, got examined petitioner No.1 - the father of the deceased as PW.1 and reiterated the petition averments and got marked the documents at Exs.P.1 to 24.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Seizer Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.6 is the Inquest Report, Ex.P.7 is the postmortem report, Ex.P.8 is the Notice u/s 133 of M. Ex.P.12 is the Bank account details of deceased, Ex.P.13 to 15 are the Notarized copies of Aadhar card of deceased and petitioners, Ex.P.16 is the Appointment Letter, Ex.P.17 to 22 are the Payslips,
Ex.P.23 is the Form No.16 and Ex.P.24 is the Identity Card.
10. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Thirumalashettahalli Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.

On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No.
69/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.
11.
Ex.P.1 to 10 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the offending vehicle driver.
After registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.10, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle U/s. 279 and 304A of IPC.
The Ex
, certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
12. On the other hand, contesting respondent i.e., Insurance Company got examined its Legal Executive as RW.1.
In his examination-in-chief RW.1 disputed the accident and contended that, his insured vehicle is not involved in the alleged accident.

But to support his contention contesting respondent except denial in the form of oral evidence he has not produced any documents to show Krishna Reddy V.V vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143859379/

sentences.text: that, offending vehicle is not involved in the accident.

Moreover, insurance company has admitted about the submission of charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and based upon that, they have taken contention that, driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
This itself shows that, insurance company not disputed about the accident.
13. In this case, none of the contesting parties failed to prove that, accident is not caused due to the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, having regard to the above facts and circumstances, this court opine that, accident is caused solely due to negligence of driver of offending Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-3518.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:

This Issue is regarding dependency, quantum of compensation to be awarded to petitioners and who is liable to pay the same, which is answered under the following heads:
15. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY: To ascertain the actual loss of dependency, the age, income of deceased and the number of dependents of the deceased are to be taken into consideration.
It is the contention of the petitioners that they are solely depending upon the income of the deceased and due to death of Naresh.
V, they have lost love and affection of the deceased.
16. The petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased Naresh.

V.
The deceased out of his income contributed to the income of family consisting of himself and petitioners herein.
Further, these petitioners being legal representatives of the deceased can very well maintain petition.
Hence, it is clear that, all the petitioners are depending upon the income of the deceased Naresh.
V. Hence, 1/2 of the income should be taken towards personal expenses of the deceased.

17. Considering recent judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Special leave petitioner (Civil No.25590/2014 dated:31.10.2016(National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others), in which it is observed that, "in case if the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation".

18. In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., & Others),
Wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, there can not be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork, as such addition on account of future prospects is admissible where in the absence of proof of income.

sentences.text: 19. The petitioners contended that, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged 26 years and was an employee at Maptec Consultancy and he was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
The petitioners have produced the postmortem report of deceased Naresh. V which is marked at Ex.P.7.
From perusal of the Ex.P.7 age of the deceased is mentioned as 27 Years as on the date of accident.

Hence,
the age of the deceased is considered as 27 years as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: In order to prove the income of the deceased, petitioners have produced the Appointment Letter at Ex.P.16, Payslips as per Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.22, Form No.16 at Ex.P.23 and Company Identity Card at Ex.P.24 and also examined Supervisor at M/s Maptec Consultancy Services Pvt. Ltd., as PW.2 who has produced documents at Ex.P.25 to Ex.P.28.
On going through these documents, it can be concluded that, deceased was drawing average salary of Rs34,000/- per month.

Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.34,000/- p.m.
20.
As per decision stated above, it is clear that, the Tribunal has to consider the future prospects on actual salary less tax and even for self employed or were engaged on fixed wages.
Admittedly, the age of the deceased is 27 years.
So 40% of future prospects is taken into consideration.

Taking into consideration of the same, if 40% is added to the income of the deceased it would be Rs.34,000/- +
40% of Rs.34,000/- is Rs.13,600/- = Rs.47,600/- per month.
Deceased is Bachelor.
Hence, 1/2 has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Income for consideration (Rs.47,600 - 23,800) is Rs.23,800/- per month.
Therefore the annual income (Rs.23,800 x 12) is Rs.2,85,600/-.
As such correct multiplier as per guidelines of Sarala Varma case would be "17".
Thus the loss of dependency works out to (Rs.2,85,600/- x 17) is Rs.48,55,200/-.
21. TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY, FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:
The petitioners have spent the amount towards shifting the dead body and performing funeral and obsequies ceremony.

In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court judgment passed in Special Leave petitioner (Civil) No.25590/2014 dated:31-10-2017 (National Insurance Co., Ltd Vs.
Pranaya Sethi and Others), wherein it is held that as far as conventional heads are concerned, the petitioners are entitled for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- and under the head of loss of estate at Rs.15,000/-.

sentences.text: 22. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
The petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents of deceased, so they are entitled for consortium for loss of "protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training".

Therefore, Rs.40,000/- each is awarded to the petitioners under the head of loss of consortium.
23.
ESCALATION OF 10% ON AMOUNT AWARDED UNDER CONVENTIONAL HEADS:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court at para No.59.8 of Judgment passed in Pranaya Sethi and others has directed to enhance the amount to be awarded under conventional heads to an extent of 10% on every 03 years.

Further more, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a decision delivered on 07.07.2021 in MFA No.101723/2017 clubbed with MFA No.104014/2016 between Smt. Viday @ Vidyashree W/o Bandu @ Dattu Koli and others Vs. Sanju S/o Veerappa Koli and another at paragraph No.16 has awarded 10% of enhanced amount on total amount awarded under conventional heads.
The Judgment in Pranya Sethi (referred supra) delivered on 31.10.2017, as such 06 years have lapsed.
Thus the petitioners are entitled for 20% enhanced amount under the above conventional heads.
While discussing above, this tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,10,000/- under conventional heads and 20% of the same comes to Rs.22,000/-.
Thus, petitioners are entitled for an amount of Rs.22,000/- under this head.

conventional heads Total Rs.49,87,200/-
Hence, this Tribunal feels to award just and proper compensation of Rs.49,87,200/- to the petitioners.
24. LIABILITY:

Learned counsel for the petitioners vehemently argued that the policy was in-force,
the insurance company cannot avoid the liability and further submitted that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation even presuming that the driver of the offending vehicle Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-3518 is not possessing the Driving License.

Per contra, the learned counsel for insurance company i.e., respondent No.1 vehemently submitted that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding the Driving License as on the date of accident and was minor, thereby owner of the Eicher Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-3518 violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation as claimed.

Learned counsel for petitioners relied upon the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka,
Kalburgi Bench in MFA No.202104/2024 dtd:19.09.2024 and requested to direct the Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount and recover it from the owner of the offending vehicle.

entities.text:
High Court of Karnataka,
Kalburgi Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This Court perused the above citation wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that,
offending vehicle driver was not holding driving license to drive the offending vehicle. But in the present case, driver of the offending vehicle was a minor.
So, this makes it clear that, driver of the offending vehicle is not qualified person so as to apply for driving license.
Therefore, the above Judgment relied by the counsel for petitioner is not applicable in case minor boy drives the vehicle and causes the accident.
Hence, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.
25. INTEREST:
As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied In a decision in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s

sentences.text: The petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are awarded with compensation of Rs.49,87,200/- with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being owner of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
After deposit of compensation amount, petitioners are entitled for apportionment in the ratio of 50:50 respectively.

After deposit of compensation amount awarded to petitioner No.1 and 2 60% of the amount shall be released in the name of petitioner No.1 and 2 and remaining 40%
shall be deposited in the name of petitioner No.1 and 2 in any Nationalized or Schedule Bank for a period of 03 years on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No. 2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioners are hereby directed to produce particulars of their Bank Account,
with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioners, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioners shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
